title: Every unhandled rejection is reported to the user as a failed save
why: Method simulation; the new failure kind lives in lib/jobs (outside the round). Worker builds the kind + a probe over classify()/troubleAnnouncement(), measures 3 walked shapes on both arms.

title: jobs.cancel rewrites a settled job as failed - settle guards, cancel does not
why: Same file as above (lib/jobs). One-line guard; instrument = drive the cancel path directly if pure, else a source ratchet the worker must seed red.

title: A forge commit that fails between its two index writes appends duplicate ledger rows on retry
why: Carry x2 lacking its instrument: a FOUNDRY_DIR root override so a commit probe never touches tracked ledger.json/styles.json. Instrument first, then measure retry -> N rows vs 2N.

title: An extract run records the style ids it kept, not the ids the catalogue actually wrote
why: Same instrument, same store files as above; one worker, second commit.

title: No gate runs the repository's Python, and the instrument now exists
why: Was `architecture` under v3.0; it is policy-tighten + out-of-scope (gates.yml). Worker adds a setup-python job running selftest.py, proves it blocks by seeding a failing case on the branch.

title: A run that gave up mid-generation still reports `done`
why: In-tree contract (RunStatus union, 3 consumers enumerable by grep) without a verifier - letters (a)-(d) are the worker's checklist. Instrument: selftest case with recycle_comfy faked to refuse.

title: Seven source-ratchet probes still carry the unsound comment stripper
why: Out-of-scope for foundry-ui, in-scope for a worker owning tests/. Before: 7 probes on the unsound pair; after: 0. Any probe that turns RED on adoption is a NEW finding the worker must report, not suppress.

title: Creating an extraction shrinks the whole gallery with no sign of progress
why: unmeasurable with a named instrument: a live-lane fixture of N images timing first feedback. Worker builds the fixture + a per-image counter; before 0 signals, after N.

title: The extract commit refuses a `failed` run that the forge commit would accept
why: POLICY CONFLICT between two rounds: 2026-09-05 called it a defect; 2026-09-06 documented EXTRACT_COMMITTABLE as 'narrower on purpose - a failed extraction has no partial artefact worth ratifying'. Only you can say whether a breaker-failed run with finished styles is committable. If yes, it is an XS + probe update.

title: The Python half of the build declares no dependencies anywhere
why: Operator-only act: the honest pin set is `pip freeze` on the GPU rig (manifest: this box is `machine: secondary`). A worker here would guess pins, which is the defect.

title: The outbox is 8 lines from its cap and nothing in this repo drains it
why: Operator-only act: ingest in the Personas app deletes the file. Round 4 cannot record its coverage until then.

title: app/_phases/research/guided/ is four files this context's map entry does not list
why: Operator-only act + architecture: a delta scan needs the bridge alive (refused all session) and CLAUDE.md forbids hand-editing the map. Five undrained lines in .vault/map-drift.md.

title: /api/recalibrate spawns an 800s Opus run with no size bound on notebook or renders
why: out-of-scope seam (app/api/recalibrate/route.ts) - only `notes` non-empty is checked (route.ts:313); /api/frames bounds beats/facts/size and its header calls the sibling bound the rule. Instrument (in scope): drive recalibratePOST with a 5MB notebook under an empty PATH and assert 413 before any CliError; then extend it to every route importing lib/claudeCli. Method today: simulation.

title: 13 of 14 guardAccessOnly routes are asserted gated by source match only, never driven for 401
why: imaging-auth's driven set is scoped to the money door on purpose; only /api/foundry/file is driven (foundry-routes probe). All 14 use `const denied = guardAccessOnly(req); if (denied) return denied;` today (walked), so the value is coverage, not a live hole. Instrument: a derived table over app/api/foundry/** driving each handler (dynamic segments adapted) with no secret -> 401. Method today: simulation.

title: A committed test.only passes the pre-push hook: forbidOnly is gated on CI and the hook does not set it
why: out-of-scope (.githooks/pre-push). playwright.config.ts states the residual gap; the hook runs `npm run verify` with no CI=1. Instrument: run the hook's verify with a seeded .only and assert it refuses. Setting CI=1 also reaches `next build` and eslint - the worker measures both arms.

title: playwright.live.config.ts says 'This lane is four journeys'; tests/live has seven
why: out-of-scope (playwright.live.config.ts:80). Copy asserting a count the tree contradicts; derive or drop the number. Before: 1 false sentence, After: 0.

title: lib/identityEviction.ts opens the database for the eviction transaction and never closes it
why: out-of-scope seam (lib/). The rule is stepStore's, the ratchet is built and LISTS this file as the one exemption (shared-notebook-contracts.probe.spec.ts::UNCLOSED), so the debt is visible and a new leak fails. The fix is a try/finally around the existing await at ~line 260; every sign-out and account switch currently leaks one connection with a live onversionchange handler. Instrument: delete the UNCLOSED entry and watch the probe go green.

title: A warning or info Notice mounts a role=status region with its text already inside, so it announces nowhere
why: ui/Notice.tsx is this context's, but the judgement call is per call site and 10 of the 12 are not. announcer.tsx's own probe states the rule this violates: 'a region rendered with its text already in it announces nowhere' — a live region must mount empty and be mutated. role=alert (severity=error) IS announced on insertion, which is why global-error.tsx uses it; role=status is not. Notice's own header claims warning/info 'appear IN RESPONSE TO AN ACTION', but 5 of 12 sites are on-load empty states where announcing would be noise. Instrument: route action-triggered sites through useAnnounce with a key, leave empty states as content; measure as cases announced of cases that should be.

title: usePhaseReport stamps the report before awaiting it, so a failed progress write is never retried
why: the stamp is written to the ref BEFORE `await reportPhase`, so a transient failure leaves the shelf and rail showing the wrong phase word for the session; the effect will not re-run because its deps are unchanged. Byte-identical in frames/useFrames.ts, which is where it was lifted from — one rule, two copies, so a fix must land in both or it is a parity defect. Resetting the ref alone changes nothing (the effect does not re-run); it needs a retry tick. Instrument: drive usePhaseReport under the hook dispatcher trailer-cut-lifecycle already uses, with reportPhase rejecting once.

title: Counter-positions render in the notebook modal and reach the triage board not at all
why: direction: giving counter-positions a card class changes what a reviewer may scope, which is a product decision about the board's vocabulary, not a repair. Run 1's strongest counter — the four-year-cycle reading, which types.ts says disproves the notebook's own `tension: high` — is readable and unscopeable. Now stated truthfully in types.ts and pinned (no card's title is a counter-position's text), so the absence is visible rather than mis-described as a protected card.
